♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! This game is so janky! There is a reason why peak player count in this game is less than 60...
The concept of the game is interesting, you are essentially only using your arms to move... which is honestly extremely restrictive and makes you HEAVILY dependent on your room size. Luckily for me I have a big room, but still, this is very bad.
The main problem with this game is that it's an earlier VR title, so you will be doing lots of things which just don't really work well, but early devs did not know that, like looking directly UP and DOWN to see the target, which is very uncomfortable, there is no way to re-center VR or turn with a stick, those features come standard with modern releases, so you will be constantly walking and turning irl and if you have a cord... good luck, lol.
The second level in the game has a hidden medal, which I REALLY wanted to get... And I got it, but I had the most miserable experience ever. First of all, it requires you to make PIXEL PERFECT jump down, so you have to move in the air and look down, all at the same time, which is very uncomfortable. Than you have to do a couple of easy jumps and than comes most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ part. You need to build up your momentum to jump across a big gap, it will take you a while to even get to it, but making this jump is almost impossible for non-veteran player, you just have to get lucky (also the momentum mechanic is taught in 4th level, crazy). So, after watching a tutorial and getting lucky, I made it across and I learned a lot about this game and how bad it is. Sometimes you jump and sometimes you don't, sometimes momentum throws you high and sometimes and it STOPS you on tiniest geometry, sometimes your hands snap to target and sometimes they miss... Is it better to move hands in the direction of the jump or put them behind you? Is it better to hold or release early to jump higher? The answer to all of these questions is "idk", the game does not know the answer to this, it's random... and random is soooo "fun" in a VR platformer where you cant even move on your own only relying on surroundings.
I honestly do not understand how this abysmal game has such positive reviews. Like... I guess if you don't care about collectables and just ♥♥♥♥ around and do time trails it could be decent, but the moment you go for collectables, you are gonna feel miserable... And this was exactly my experience. 
Maybe a better VR headset would also help, since I feel like FOV is extremely important in this game, since often times you have to grab objects off screen.
4/10, just for the novelty.

[h1]Reseña del Videojuego: ¡A Escalar se ha Dicho, TO THE TOP!

[h2]Resumen:
¡Bienvenidos, queridos y valientes escaladores virtuales! Hoy en mi rincón sarcástico y digital, vamos a hablar de TO THE TOP, un juego que hace sentir esos vértigos y mariposas en la barriga sin moverse del sillón. Ideal para quienes aman las alturas, pero prefieren mantener sus pies bien pegados al suelo de la sala.

[h2]Aspectos importantes e interesantes:
Lo primero que hay que decir es que TO THE TOP no es para los débiles de corazón... ni para los que se marean fácil con realidad virtual. Lo genial del juego es cómo usa el movimiento de tus manitas virtuales para hacerte sentir como un Spiderman de pacotilla. Mientras más alto subes, más desafiante se vuelve todo, y hay que admitir que es un subidón de adrenalina (¿entendieron? Subidón... porque es de escalar).

Y no, esto no es simplemente escalar bloques aburridos, los niveles están diseñados con ciudades flotantes, templos en el aire y hasta ruinas antiguas que parece que fueron diseñadas por un Indiana Jones aficionado.

[h2]Aspectos por mejorar:
A ver, que sí, TO THE TOP es divertido, pero tampoco vamos a ignorar que a veces los controles pueden hacerte sentir que estás intentando escalar con mantequilla en las manos. ¿Y la historia? Bueno, parece que se quedó en el segundo piso porque no subió mucho en calidad.

Y aunque los escenarios son variados, después de un rato, te preguntas si realmente necesitas escalar otro monolito que parece un primo lejano del anterior.

※クライミングゲームだと思ったあなた、違いますよ。

そしてチェックポイントの間隔が長い。ミスするとかなり前まで戻される事もあり、間違ってリトライボタンに触れた時なんかは心が折れそう。

I guess the game is okay if you play solo ... from what I've seen it's midway between Climbey and Windland, not as physical as Climbey, not as exciting as Windland. It's the bigmac of haute cuisine if you want. It has the right ingredient for the most part but it's kind of bland. It might get better, but as I bought it for the multiplayer aspect and ...

... just completely ignore the fact that there is multiplayer. It is beyond basic in the way it is implemented : you can not choose the level you want to play, let alone open a "friend's only" room. If someone ... *anyone* ... already opened a multiplayer room you will just be thrown in (unless  nobody else is playing in which case you might be able to choose the level after all). This means that you HAVE to play with strangers if any is playing a multiplayer game and that, if you get the chance to open your own room, rando's *will* join.
Additionally the time limit must be beaten by everybody, which means that if you are a noob you will spoil the level for people better than you as they NEED you to finish it in a timely manner, and vice versa.

The worst part of all that though is that people asked the devs about it, and instead of fixing this obvious flaw they let it be known that they *might* correct it in "To The Top 2". That's just showing a disdain for your own customers that is only matched by EA microtransactions. 

yeah ... I refunded.

Забавная игрушечка, симулятор паркура. Очень энергичная. В тайных местах, куда только с разбега или с распрыга заскочить можно, напрятаны секреты. Тех, у кого руки длинные да загребущие, порадует магазин с костюмами. Для всех без исключения есть канаты и перила, возможность постоять на выпущенной стреле башенного крана или сигануть через пропасть. В некоторых местах можно постоять и поцелиться, а некоторые нужно проходить сходу, на скорости. Да, игрушка, можно сказать, немного приотстала в графике, ить сколько лет назад над ней старались (вот тут не согрешить, что старались), но упрощенная графика в данном случае скорее плюс. И вот почему – когда вы проходите уровни на лету, сразу видно, за что нужно цепляться и откуда не выбраться.

Сложность прохождения, как заведено, идет по нарастающей. Хотя не без фокусов. Мне, например, так и не удалось на отлично пройти самый первый уровень. Не хватает каких-то десятых секунд, хоть ты тресни. А вот после середины я уже потерял интерес из-за необходимости быть постоянно начеку. Но это, что касается меня, так как я не экстремал.

К покупке могу рекомендовать по скидке. Несмотря на все плюшки, которыми творцы пытались обогатить TO THE TOP и аккуратное исполнение, игра скучновата, требует определенного настроя, большого пространства и, несомненно, сил.

It doesn't provide much information as you can see from the negative reviews, but that being said, if you have a 360 degree tracking area and are able to turn whilst you play, this is a fun movement game. One of my favorite games for VR. I love the way they designed the platforming. Jumping around and finding a way to the goal is very fun, and often times there's more than one way to get to the end faster than you did before. I'm glad they went with the locomotion they did, you don't have to swing your arms around like other VR platformers, it's more about being quick and precise with where you're aiming. With each consecutive jump, you jump even further, which really gets your momentum going. Where you're looking also matters, your momentum follows your head movement somewhat.

It's also worth mentioning that this game doesn't seem to induce motion sickness as easily as some other fast-paced games. I'd compare it to Jet Island in terms of comfort, maybe even a bit better.

The levels are all really well designed, definitely fun enough to repeat a bunch of times to get the best score you can. The balance between difficulty and speed, the pacing, it's all perfect. There are all sorts of hidden gems to find, which will help you unlock more levels and customization items. The levels also feel pretty unique from one another, I never felt like there were any "repeats" in the levels, and the creativity in their designs is excellent.

I can't give a review for this game without mentioning the music. The soundtrack goes fantastically well with this game, with chill, upbeat songs. It really sounds like the game developers asked local artists for some good tracks to put in the game. It's always a talking point when I show somebody the game for the first time.

The game is also optimized very well. Never had any performance problems, and for people with beefier systems, you can crank your settings up to 120hz-144hz and the game feels that much more smooth. In VR games, there's a balance between good graphics and good framerate/stability that I think the developers have found perfectly.

So all in all, this game is a solid 10/10 from me.
I have a lot of VR games and this is definitely one of the best experiences you can have in VR.

[h1]Quick Summary[/h1]
To The Top is a different kind of climbing game. The mechanics are a bit more like leaping from surface to surface instead of the expected hand-over-hand movement. The courses are fun, challenging, and plentiful for the style of play. If you're looking for a game focused on mobility, think about picking this one up!

[h1]My Full Review[/h1]
Overall, I do recommend this game to anyone looking for a challenging VR platformer. The gameplay is simple enough to grasp, but hard to master. There are some hidden secrets to find and cosmetics to unlock, but can be skipped if you're not into that kind of thing.

I spent time getting 100% completion on the time trials and secrets. It was fun, but sometimes more frustrating to go that route than to just enjoy the basic gameplay.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The mechanics are simple and work well for the courses provided. There's a nice selection of courses that challenge you in different ways and introduce new obstacles as your progress. What I like the most is that a good selection of the levels provide a few different ways to get to the finish line, and it's up to you to find which route is the fastest.

[h1]Story / Plot[/h1]
Generally, there isn't one. This is a gameplay-focused game with a little bit of lore to give you a sense of the world. Otherwise, don't expect anything groundbreaking here.

[h1]Graphics / Audio[/h1]
The soundtrack sticks out as unique and kind of unexpected. The tracks work pretty well for the "open and free" feeling that this game tries to go for, however they might lean a bit to far into "music taste" instead of a game theme for some. You'll notice the sound effects are reminiscent of retro platforming games which is a nice touch. They're fun, lighthearted, and cartoony.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
To The Top is a great mobility game that's easy to pick up, but hard to master. If you're enthusiastic about mobility focused games, you'll find that in this title. Even after completing this game to 100%, it still never fails to pump the adrenaline.

I'm slightly prone to motion sickness, and expected, picking up a VR parkour game, that I'd need to refund it.

Instead, I found myself delighted by the freedom of movement as I bounced from wall to wall, trying to beat my best times and scouring the map for hidden collectibles. I don't know what the developers did, but I have never enjoyed simulated falling quite as much. If I had a guess, it's because your jump direction and angle are always based on where you are looking, not any controller input, making the movements feel more natural.

I haven't played any of the (many) other VR parkour games on the market, but To the Top really grew on me. I initially didn't care for the indie-rock-techno-adjacent songs, but I eventually came to like how they felt like they were taking me on a journey. I initially found the controls a bit unintuitive and frustrating, but soon keyed into the flow of it and felt like a graceful flying squirrel.

Importantly, there's a good amount of content here for a VR game. Unlocking all of the customizations (and achievements) requires 140 medals, which took me around 10 hours to do. 100% completing the game would take a bit longer (some of the levels are *hard*), where as just sprinting to the credits would probably take 5 or 6 hours.

There's also multiplayer, but I haven't tried it. This game's single player is good enough that it's just a nice bonus.
